LIGHT TRANSDUCERS
OBJECTIVES
w Describe the ratings of light sources.
w Describe the ratings of light sensors.
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
In this lesson, you will learn about opto-electronic devices, light transducers.
INTRODUCTIONM
These devices, when combined with common electronic circuits, produce light circuits that have many uses.
For example, in communications, light is used to send information over fiber optic cables.
Because of the very high frequencies of light, more information can be sent. Light waves allow much larger information bandwidths..
Light circuits are also used in cameras, audio equipment, and in measuring devices.
Lasers operate using light. The word laser is an acronym meaning Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.
Let's Begin the Lesson on LIGHT TRANSDUCERS...............................
LESSON MENU
Light transmitters are either incandescent or luminescent..
DISCUSSION
DEFINITION
DEFINITION
LUMINESCENT - Luminescent describes light sources that emit light without heat, such as Light Emitting Diodes.
Manufacturers specify all light transmitter outputs in two major areas, wavelength and amount of light.
Wavelength is normally given in microns or angstroms. Wavelength is important when matching transmitters to receivers.
DEFINITION
MICRONS - A micron is 1 x 10-6 meters. It is used to describe the short wavelengths of light.
DEFINITION
ANGSTROMS - An angstrom is 1 x 10-10 meters. It is used to describe the short wavelengths of light.
A typical light bulb produces both photometric and radiometric energy.
A typical light bulb produces both photometric and radiometric energy.
PHOTOMETRIC - Photometric energy is visible light between 0.4 and 0.8 microns, or 4,000 to 8,000 angstroms.
DEFINITION
RADIOMETRIC - Radiometric energy is non-visible light in the ultraviolet and infrared ranges.
DEFINITION
On the other hand, LEDs can produce only one type of energy at a time. LEDs can produce either photometric or radiometric energy..
When choosing a light source, the wavelength must be known.
The total amount of light produced by a light transmitter device is also important to know.
The rating is called candlepower, or cd for short.
Candlepower compares to an ordinary wax candle as a reference.
For example, if a light source outputs 5 cd, it would be roughly equivalent to 5 wax candles aligned with the wicks intertwined.
Another measure of total output of a light source is Lumens,
To convert between candlepower and lumens, you divide or multiply by 12.56.
For example, a 100 cd light source has a lumens rating of 1256.
Candlepower and lumens are measures of total output. You have probably noticed that the farther away from you a light source is its intensity is less......
The unit of measure for light illumination or intensity is called footcandles. The intensity decreases with the square of the distance.
For example, a light source that has a total output of 100 cd has an intensity of 1 footcandle at 10 feet.
The last rating of a light source is the photometric output power measured in watts.
Photometric output power is similar to electrical power and is used in calculating the sensitivity of light receivers.

The incandescent transmitter is an ordinary light bulb.

The output shown for 2870 Kelvin is the standard used by industry for rating incandescent lamps.

The light emitting diode, LED has revolutionized the
LED's produce light without using heat and are symbolized as shown.
LED's have advantages over incandescent lamps: RAPHICS TEXT) * Increased efficiency * Narrow frequency outputs * Sharp colors * Rugged, small and inexpensive
However, the disadvantages to LEDs are: RAPHICS TEXT)Low intensity output Limited color selection Low breakdown ratings
LED's operate on the same principle as an ordinary diode...
When forward biased, current flows through the device.
The free electrons and holes combine, providing current flow.
The difference in a LED is that the doping of the crystal is specially manufactured.
When holes and electrons combine, energy is released in the form of light.
The light is then physically directed to the surface of the diode and is focused through a lens.
Manufacturing techniques allow for red, yellow, amber, green and infrared light outputs.
As you can see, the voltage necessary to overcome the barrier potential of the PN junction is higher in LED's than ordinary silicon or germanium diodes.
Also, the breakdown voltage, reverse bias or Vr, is lower for LED's, around 3 volts.
These voltages, or ratings, are given in reference books for each type of LED and should not be exceeded.
Finally, comparing an LED to an incandescent lamp, you can see that LEDs produce narrow wavelengths or specific colors.
The incandescent lamp produces large wavelengths or white light...

Light receivers are either resistive, current, or voltage devices.
DISCUSSION
Light receivers, as light transmitters, are rated by the manufacturer.
Which rating measures the intensity or illumination of a light source?
DEFINITION
MICRONS - A micron is 1 x 10-6 meters. It is used to describe the short wavelengths of light.
DEFINITION
ANGSTROMS - An angstrom is 1 x 10-10 meters. It is used to describe the short wavelengths of light.
If the wavelength of a receiver does not overlap the wavelength of a transmitter, a light system will not operate.
A second rating is the sensitivity of the light receiver...
Each type of light receiver will react to the amount of light received and the wavelength of the light in different ways.
The ratings can be given in footcandles, watts, or in irradiance (H).
Irradiance is the light energy at the surface of a receiver.
H equals the power output of a light transmitter divided by 12.56 times the distance between the transmitter and receiver squared.
It is similar to footcandles of a light transmitter. The 12.56 is used because P is calculated from lumens and lumens equals 12.56 times candlepower..
If the irradiance of the received light is below the sensitivity of a light receiver, the receiver will not detect the light.
For example, if a light source produces 2,562 lumens and the receiver is ten feet from the source, H is .003 or 3 mH.
2, 562 Lumens = 3.77 Watts (P = Lumens/680)
If the light receiver is rated at .005 or 5 mH, the receiver will not detect the light.
The last rating of a light receiving device is memory......
When a light receiver is brought from a dark or bright light condition to a new level, the device reacts slowly.
The output, either resistance changes, current changes, or voltage changes, takes time to arrive at the new level.
Also, light receivers tend to overshoot the new level before settling to the new value of resistance, current or voltage output.
The amount of memory, given in time, limits the use of light receivers.
If the memory in a certain device is long, it can not be used in frequency applications (such as modulation) above 10 Hz.
If the memory in a certain device is short, noise will interfere with its operation.
Normally, the wavelength and memory of a light device is given in reference books. The irradiance is also calculated and listed.

Irradiance is the amount of radiant energy at a devices surface. It is not the reaction time of a light receiver.

Now, let's look at four common light receivers...............
The simplest and oldest light receiver is the photocell (also called a cadmium cell or photoconductive cell).
The photocell, symbolized as shown, operates by the device changing its resistance according to the intensity of light.
Note that most resistive materials are sensitive to light.m
The energy in light causes the electrons in a resistive material to gain energy, thus lowering the materials resistance.
The more intense the light, the more energy the electrons pick up, material resistance decreases.
Cadmium Sulfide (CdS) and Cadmium Selenite (CdSe) are two materials that exhibit the most change and are used in photocells.
By placing the photocell in a circuit, the changing resistance of the photocell effects current flow and the voltage dropped across the load resistor.tor.
When the intensity of light increases, the photocell resistance decreases, increasing current and E ..
When the intensity of light decreases, the photocell resistance increases, decreasing current and E .
The response of cadmium photocells to light is nearly identical to the human eye.
What type of light receiver is the photocell?

Although voltage in a photocell circuit changes according to the amount of light received, the photocell does not operate by changing the circuit voltage. The changing voltage is the result of the photocells operation.
TRY AGAIN!

Although voltage in a photocell circuit changes according to the amount of light received, the photocell does not operate by changing the circuit voltage. The changing voltage is the result of the photocells operation.
TRY AGAIN!
The next three devices are solid state light receivers. Let's look at the photodiode first.
The photodiode, symbolized as shown, is a specially designed silicon diode that changes current flow according to the intensity of light.
The photodiode is reversed biased when the depletion region is illuminated.
As in any diode when reverse biased, a small amount of reverse current flows.
The amount of reverse current in a photodiode depends on the amount of light striking the depletion region.
The light energy which enters the depletion region causes more electrons and holes to combine. Thus increasing the reverse current flow.
The reverse current flow depends on the amount of light received.
The response of a photodiode is a lot broader than a photocell and can be used with a number of light transmitters.
What type of light receiver is the photodiode?

The photodiode operates using reverse current flow. Technically, the resistance of the diode does change but, it is the reverse current flow that changes according to the amount of light striking the device.
TRY AGAIN!
A photodiode requires an external voltage source that reverse biases the device. Voltage does not change according to how much light is received.
TRY AGAIN!
The third solid state light receiver is the photovoltaic...
The photovoltaic, symbolized as shown, is also a diode that changes voltage according to the intensity of light.
The photovoltaic operates without bias with the depletion region illuminated.
As light energy strikes the PN junction, it causes the minority carriers to migrate to the different materials of the diode.
The electrons cause a negative charge in the N material and the holes cause a positive charge in the P material.
This sets up different charges and the diode acts as a battery.
The charges then can sustain current flow to an external load.
In other words, E is proportional to the radiant energy striking the PN junction.
The response of a photovoltaic is the same as the photodiode.
What type of light receiver is the photovoltaic?
The photovoltaic operates by the minority carriers charging the P and N material differently. The photocell operates by resistance.
TRY AGAIN!
The photovoltaic operates by the minority carriers charging the P and N material differently. The photodiode operates by current.
TRY AGAIN!
The last solid state light receiver is the phototransistor.
The phototransistor, symbolized as shown, is a transistor that changes emitter and collector current according to the intensity of light.
The phototransistor is similar to a normal NPN transistor except the base is sensitive to light.
As light energy strikes the base of the phototransistor, it causes changes in base current.
Changes in base current cause the emitter to collector current to change.
In other words, collector current is proportional to the radiant energy striking the transistor base.
The response of a phototransistor is the same as the photodiode and photovoltaic.
What type of light receiver is the phototransistor?
The phototransistor operates by light changing the base current which effects the transistors operation. A photocell operates by resistance changes.
TRY AGAIN!
The phototransistor operates by light changing the base current which effects the transistors operation. A photovoltaic operates by voltage changes.
TRY AGAIN!
This completes the information on RECEIVERS.2 TITLE........
1. Light receivers are either resistance, current, or voltage devices.
2. Irradiance is the light energy at the surface of a receiver.
3. Memory is the reaction of a light receiver to changes in the amount of light intensity..
4. A photocell operates by light changing the resistance of the resistive material.
5. A photodiode operates by light changing the reverse current flow.
6. A photovoltaic operates by light setting up different charges that act as a battery.
7. A phototransistor operates by light changing the base current which changes the emitter and collector currents.
